Definition: a primary verb; to live (literally or figuratively):--life(-time), (a-)live(-ly), quick.
BiblicalUsage: Zao is to live, and in the New Testament it carries the whole weight of real life. Matthew 4:4 says, "Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God." In Mark 5:23 a father begs Jesus to come "that she may be healed; and she shall live." Luke 2:36 shows Anna, who had lived with a husband seven years and then served God in the temple for decades, and in John 4:10 Jesus offers the Samaritan woman living water."
TheologicalSignificance: I believe zao is the promise of the gospel in one verb. I hold that the life Jesus gives is not just breath and years, it is life fed by every word of God, as Matthew 4:4 says, and water that never runs dry, as John 4:10 promises. My position is that zao is the difference between merely existing and truly living, and that life is found only in him.
